title: Reduce GPU memory & workspace usage: activation checkpointing, scratch buffer pooling, and arena tuning
author: Marina Costa
description: Motivation: we observed recurring OOMs and high transient peak memory on long-sequence workloads (tokens > 8k) in production; this PR reduces peak GPU memory and workspace allocations with three complementary changes: 1) opt-in activation checkpointing for transformer blocks with a per-model heuristic to limit CPU/GPU recompute cost; 2) pooled scratch buffer allocator + reuse across attention/kernel paths to reduce temporary workspace allocations and fragmentation; 3) arena tuning for the device allocator to keep working set resident and lower peak fragmentation overhead. Changes include new runtime flags, a model-config heuristic, unit and integration tests, and perf regressions for a few small kernels addressed with kernel tiling tweaks. Checklist: implement feature flags and default heuristics, add tests, update docs, run perf suite, validate against k8s Dedicated/GPU CI images. Testing summary and validation below.

bench_results: Long-sequence (12k tokens) peak GPU memory before: 48.2 GB, after: 36.1 GB (~25% reduction)
End-to-end p95 latency (single-request, 12k tokens) before: 1.12s, after: 1.16s (+4%), acceptable due to reduced OOMs and higher success rate
Throughput (continuous batching, batch-window 20ms) improved 1.15x under heavy tail loads due to lower temporary workspace churn
Scratch buffer reuse eliminated ~1.8GB transient allocations on median request path
Activation checkpointing recompute overhead measured at 8-12% CPU/GPU extra compute for large models but reduced peak memory by ~9-14% per run depending on layer depth
Arena tuning reduced fragmentation spikes by ~30% on synthetic allocation traces

release_notes: Reduced peak GPU memory and workspace allocations for large-sequence workloads via activation checkpointing (opt-in), pooled scratch buffers, and arena tuning. Expected benefits: fewer OOMs, improved success rate for long sequences, and lower per-token transient memory. Tradeoffs: small latency increase when checkpointing is enabled; defaults conservative (checkpointing off for small models).
merge_commit_message:
Reduce GPU memory & workspace usage: activation checkpointing, scratch buffer pooling, arena tuning

- Add arena tuning knobs
- Add pooled scratch allocator
- Opt-in activation checkpointing with model heuristic
- Tests and docs
notes_for_release: Ops: for Dedicated clusters, recommended to enable scratch_pool globally. For Hosted, leave activation_checkpointing OFF by default; platform team will opt-in high-memory customers after validation.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: checkpointing may increase p50/p95 for small inference shapes. Mitigation: heuristic keeps checkpointing off for small models; feature flag allows rollout via canary and A/B. Scratch buffer pooling added with tests to avoid cross-stream races.
